Optional and off by default. Needs root. Lasts until reboot and can be switched off here at any time. Restart the chosen apps afterwards.

Turns decryption off, undoes the system-wide trust, deletes the certificate key and the app list, and records that you withdrew consent. Captured content is kept until you delete it. Also remove the user certificate in Settings → Security if you installed it.
Banking, payment, government, password-manager and system apps are not listed and can never be added.

WAYD will act as a middleman for the apps you choose so it can read their encrypted traffic. This may expose passwords, messages, payment details and other sensitive content — to WAYD on this phone only.

• Most apps refuse user-installed certificates; those apps will be shown as “metadata only”.
• Some apps may stop working while this is on.
• Anyone who obtains WAYD’s certificate key could intercept your traffic. WAYD stores it encrypted and deletes it when you turn this off.
• Never enable this on a phone you don’t own or for people who haven’t agreed.

1. What WAYD collects
Traffic metadata (apps, hosts, sizes, times), cleartext and — for the apps you choose — decrypted request and response content, app permission-use history, and facts about installed apps.

2. Where it is stored
Only on this device, in an encrypted database, excluded from backups. The certificate key is encrypted with a key held by the Android Keystore.

3. What WAYD sends off the device
Nothing. The only network use is what you start yourself, such as downloading a model or a database.

4. Retention
Decrypted content stays until you delete it (Danger zone → Delete captured content) or turn the feature off and wipe data.

5. Export and wipe
You can delete captured content at any time. “Disable and remove CA” removes the certificate key, the app list and any system-wide trust.

6. Other people’s information
Decrypted traffic can contain information about other people (for example messages). You are responsible for using this lawfully and only on devices and accounts you are entitled to inspect.

7. Version
Statement version 1.

This uses root to make Android’s system trust store include WAYD’s certificate. Apps that ignore user certificates will then accept it, which lets WAYD read their traffic.

While it is on, anyone with WAYD’s certificate key could impersonate any website to this phone, and some apps may misbehave. Nothing is installed permanently: the change is undone by a reboot or by switching this off.

Only continue on a phone you own.
